title: Shoes off, right foot in
hook: shoes at the door, enter with the right foot, a greeting prayer on the lips

segments.voice: Yesterday: masjid, the place of prostration, and a school, shelter and town square too. Your line was a place to bow.

A row of shoes by a front door says a lot about a house. A neat rack in a friend's hallway. A basket of slippers. Grandma's mat, where nobody gets past in sneakers. Step out of your shoes and you step out of the outside world, literally, and your feet land on something softer. At a mosque door the pile is bigger: a long shelf, or just a heap, of sneakers, loafers, tiny children's sandals, work boots. That pile is the first thing a visitor meets. Today: shoes off, right foot in.
screen: `SHOES AT GRANDMA'S DOOR.` → `STEPPING OUT OF THE OUTSIDE.` → `A PILE OF SHOES AT THE MOSQUE.`

segments.voice: Why shoes off? The simplest answer is the floor. In a mosque, people put their foreheads on that carpet five times a day, and you wouldn't walk across a kitchen table in the shoes you wore through a parking lot. It isn't that shoes are forbidden in prayer as such. Bukhari reports that the companion Anas was asked whether the Prophet ﷺ ever prayed in his sandals, and he said yes; scholars add that the sandals must be clean. But on a shared carpet, shoes off is the custom. Then the right foot. Aisha said, in Bukhari, that the Prophet liked to begin with the right in everything he could: putting on his sandals, combing his hair, washing for prayer. So it's customary to step into the mosque right foot first, and out left foot first. A small thing that turns an ordinary doorway into a moment you notice. Then the words. Sahih Muslim reports the Prophet teaching that on entering the mosque one says: Allahumma iftah li abwaba rahmatik. O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy. And on leaving: O Allah, I ask You for Your bounty. Mercy inside, bounty outside. For a visitor, a few more things help. Modest, loose clothes. Mosques may ask women to cover their hair, and some keep scarves at the door. Speak softly. And don't walk directly in front of someone who's praying; wait, or go around behind them. None of it is a test. It's what you do at grandma's: you come in gently.
screen: `SHOES OFF: FACES GO ON THIS FLOOR.` · `THE RIGHT FOOT FIRST.` · `OPEN FOR ME THE DOORS OF YOUR MERCY.` · `DON'T CROSS IN FRONT OF SOMEONE PRAYING.` · then, large: `COME IN GENTLY.`

segments.voice: Walk to the nearest doorway, slipping off your shoes if it's easy, and pause at the threshold for one breath. Step through right foot first, and let the left follow. If you pray, you can say as you step, Allahumma iftah li abwaba rahmatik; if not, just notice the change: the air, the floor, the sound.
Shoes off. The first step into a mosque: shoes at the door, the right foot first, and a request for the doors of mercy. Today's word.
Your line: come in gently. Mercy on the way in, bounty on the way out. See you tomorrow.
